result: In 289 ME/CFS clinic patients, percent-predicted peak VO2 fell with ICC severity grade (90% mild, 64% moderate, 48% severe), as did VT VO2 (47/38/30%), steps/day (8235/5195/2031) and SF-36 physical function (70/43/15).
reason: Same CPET peak VO2 measure; adds a severity gradient (no control group).

result: N-back fMRI activation was equal before exercise; after exercise ME/CFS showed increased activation in dorsal midbrain, left Rolandic operculum and right middle insula, GWI showed midbrain/vermis deactivation, and controls were unchanged.
reason: Independent exercise-provocation fMRI, but different task and regions (not parietal/cingulate), so extends rather than replicates.

result: Cluster analysis of resting autonomic (Task Force Monitor) and arterial stiffness measures in 131 Fukuda CFS patients gave four profiles (34% sympathetic-dysautonomia, 5% sympathetic, 21% parasympathetic, 40% sympathovagal balance); the sympathetic-dysautonomia group had the most severe disease and lowest quality of life.
reason: Resting HRV-based autonomic subgrouping with severity link; no controls, so a subgroup extension only.

result: In 45 Fukuda ME/CFS vs 27 controls, T1w/T2w ratio was elevated (no decreases) in white matter and subcortical grey matter, with voxel clusters in brainstem and projection tracts, and abnormal regressions with HRV, cognition and respiration rate.
reason: Altered brainstem signal fits the finding's 'altered signal' claim; Griffith group, 2020 paper not already cited; brainstem is a minor part of the result.

result: In 45 Fukuda ME/CFS vs 27 controls, T1w/T2w ratio was elevated in white matter and subcortical grey matter (myelin/iron), with no decreased regions.
reason: T1w/T2w myelin/iron mapping is not grey-matter volume or routine clinical read; no index finding covers T1w/T2w (diffusion finding is a different measure); brainstem part covered by neuro-brainstem link.

result: Systematic review of 19 case-control studies (1995-2020) of mitochondrial structure, DNA/RNA, respiration, metabolites and coenzymes found results too inconsistent to establish a mitochondrial role in ME/CFS.
reason: A review, not an independent cohort; supports the finding's conflicting-results status rather than replicating a measure.

result: Systematic review of 19 case-control studies of mitochondrial changes found inconsistent results across studies.
reason: Review of mitochondrial measures generally, not muscle biopsy histology/fibre type; covered by the immune-cell-mito link.

result: Plasma UPLC-MS/MS proteomics in 39 ME/CFS vs 41 controls found ME/CFS associated with IGHV3-23/30 immunoglobulin levels (and IGKV3-11 in those without IBS), with ML protein panels giving AUC 0.77-0.84.
reason: Protein-level IGHV3-23/30 association supports IGHV3-30 skew via a different method (not BCR sequencing, no clonality test), so extends not replicates.

result: In 128 ME/CFS patients, N-back accuracy fell from before to within 5 min after a 30-min head-up tilt (2-back 77% to 62%, 3-back 57% to 41%).
reason: Same working-memory measure; adds persistence of orthostatic cognitive impairment after tilt (no control group).
